text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Just 26 percent of a total of 13,022 students who wrote the higher and international general certificate of secondary education exams, may achieve admission to the University of Namibia or the Polytechnic. Less than one percent qualified for entry into South African universities, provincial results show.
- Two businessmen accused of fraud over the upgrading of the single quarters at Katutura are likely to be granted bail in the Windhoek magistrate's court.
- A bilateral agreement between Namibia and South Africa to write off Namibia's N$700 million colonial debt is still outstanding after talks earlier this month.
- The process of choosing the election modus for local authority elections in December has started with angry exchanges between government and opposition parties.
